{{short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:Burkholder.jpg|thumb|Donald Burkholder]]
'''Donald Lyman Burkholder''' (January 19, 1927 – April 14, 2013<ref name="NGobit">[http://www.news-gazette.com/obituaries/2013-04-17/donald-burkholder.html Donald Burkholder (obituary)], [[The News-Gazette (Champaign-Urbana)|The News-Gazette]], April 17, 2013. Accessed April 17, 2013</ref>) was an American mathematician known for his contributions to [[probability theory]], particularly the theory of [[Martingale (probability theory)|martingales]]. The [[Quadratic variation#Martingales|Burkholder–Davis–Gundy inequality]] is co-named after him. Burkholder spent most of his professional career as a professor in the Department of Mathematics of the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]. After his retirement in 1998, Donald Burkholder remained a professor emeritus in the Department of Mathematics of the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] and a CAS Professor Emeritus of Mathematics at the Center for Advanced Study, [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]. He was a member of the [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]] and a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref> His son, [[J. Peter Burkholder]], is Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Musicology at [[Indiana University Bloomington]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Obituary: Donald L. Burkholder, 1927–2013 |url=https://imstat.org/2013/05/16/obituary-donald-l-burkholder-1927-2013/ |website=Institute of Mathematical Statistics |date=May 16, 2013 |access-date=August 22, 2026}}</ref>

==Biographical data==

Burkholder received a PhD in statistics in 1955 from the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], under the direction of [[Wassily Hoeffding]].<ref>[http://stat-or.unc.edu/programs/statistics/recentphds Ph.D.s in Statistics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100510062544/http://stat-or.unc.edu/programs/statistics/recentphds |date=2010-05-10 }}, Department of Statistics and Operations Research, [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. Accessed January 2010</ref>
He was appointed an assistant professor in the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] in 1955<ref>''News and Notices'', [[The American Mathematical Monthly]], Vol. 63, No. 2 (Feb., 1956), pp. 137-141</ref> where he remained until his retirement in 1998.<ref name="mt98">[http://www.math.uiuc.edu/mathtimes/MathTimesSP98.pdf Math Times] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605025932/http://www.math.uiuc.edu/mathtimes/MathTimesSP98.pdf |date=2011-06-05 }}, Spring 1998 issue, Department of Mathematics, [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]. Accessed January 12, 2010.</ref> He was promoted to associate professor in 1960,<ref>''News and Notices'', [[The American Mathematical Monthly]], Vol. 68, No. 3 (Mar., 1961), pp. 313-318</ref> became a professor in the department in 1964 and  was appointed as professor at the Center for Advanced Study at UIUC in 1978.<ref name="mt98"/>

Burkholder delivered an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited lecture at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1970,  a Wald Lecture at the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 1971, a  Mordell Lecture at  [[Cambridge University]] in  1986, and a Zygmund Lecture at the  [[University of Chicago]] in 1988.<ref name="fh"/>

Donald Burkholder was elected a member of the [[U.S. National Academy of Sciences]] in 1992.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1992/05/10/us/59-are-chosen-for-national-academy-of-sciences.html?pagewanted=1 59 Are Chosen for National Academy of Sciences.]  ''[[The New York Times]]'', May 10, 1992. Accessed January 12, 2010.</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110604020520/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/1007159299?pg=vprof&mbr=1002012&returl=http:%2F%2Fwww.nasonline.org%2Fsite%2FDir%2F1007159299%3Fpg=srch&view=basic&retmk=search_again_link Burkholder, Donald L. bio page], [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]]. Accessed January 12, 2010. Election citation: "During the last twenty years, Burkholder has been the leader in martingale transforms and applications of probabilistic methods to a large variety of areas in analysis, such as harmonic and analytic functions, singular integrals and Banach space classifications. He obtained wide and striking extensions of Paley's ideas in harmonic analysis of more than 30 years before."</ref> The same year he was elected a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>[http://www.math.uiuc.edu/mathtimes/MathTimesFA92.pdf Math Times] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605025827/http://www.math.uiuc.edu/mathtimes/MathTimesFA92.pdf |date=2011-06-05 }}, Fall 1992 issue, Department of Mathematics, [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]], p. 4</ref> On December 20, 2010, Burkholder was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] for "distinguished contributions to probability theory, particularly the theory of martingales, and his work in stochastic processes, [[functional analysis]], and [[Fourier analysis]]."<ref>[http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2011/0111fellows.shtml AAAS Members Elected as Fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121028132953/http://www.aaas.org/news/releases/2011/0111fellows.shtml |date=2012-10-28 }},  [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. Accessed January 13, 2011</ref><ref>[http://news.illinois.edu/news/11/0111aaasfellow_burkholder.html Illinois mathematician elected fellow of AAAS], News Bureau, [[University of Illinois]]. Accessed January 13, 2011</ref>

In 2009 Burkholder was named a SIAM Fellow by the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] ''"for advances in martingale transforms and applications of probabilistic methods in analysis"''.<ref>[http://bulletin.imstat.org/pdf/38/5 SIAM announces new Fellows.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100507175915/http://bulletin.imstat.org/pdf/38/5 |date=2010-05-07 }} IMS Bulletin, vol. 38 (2009), no. 5, [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]. Accessed January 12, 2010</ref><ref>[http://www.siam.org/about/news-siam.php?id=1545  SIAM names 193 Fellows for key contributions to applied mathematics and computational science.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110809070539/http://www.siam.org/about/news-siam.php?id=1545 |date=2011-08-09 }} News of SIAM, May 1, 2009, [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]. Accessed January 12, 2010</ref>

Burkholder was an editor (1964–1967) of the journal ''[[Annals of Mathematical Statistics]]''.<ref>[http://www.imstat.org/officials/past_editors.html Past Editors of IMS Journals.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303211512/http://www.imstat.org/officials/past_editors.html |date=2016-03-03 }}  [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]. Accessed January 12, 2010</ref> He served as the president of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 1975–76.<ref name="fh">[http://www.math.uiuc.edu/People/facultyhonors.html Faculty Honors.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110109052522/http://www.math.uiuc.edu/People/facultyhonors.html |date=2011-01-09 }} Department of Mathematics, [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]. Accessed January 12, 2010.</ref> He is a Fellow of the  [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].<ref>[http://www.imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm IMS Fellows], {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302125855/http://www.imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm |date=2014-03-02 }} [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]. Accessed January 2010.</ref>

==Selected publications==
*Burkholder, D. L.; Gundy, Richard F.,  ''Extrapolation and interpolation of quasi-linear operators on martingales''. [[Acta Mathematica]], vol. 124 (1970), pp.&nbsp;249–304
*Burkholder, Donald L., ''Inequalities for operators on martingales''. Actes du Congrès International des Mathématiciens (Nice, 1970), Tome 2, pp.&nbsp;551–557. Gauthier-Villars, Paris, 1971.
*Burkholder, Donald L., ''Distribution function inequalities for martingales'', Annals of Probability,  vol. 1 (1973), pp.&nbsp;19–42
*Burkholder, Donald L., ''A geometrical characterization of Banach spaces in which martingale difference sequences are unconditional''. Annals of Probability, vol. 9 (1981), no. 6, pp.&nbsp;997–1011
*Burkholder, Donald L., ''Explorations in martingale theory and its applications''. École d'Été de Probabilités de Saint-Flour XIX-1989, pp.&nbsp;1–66, Lecture Notes in Mathematics, vol. 1464, [[Springer-Verlag]], Berlin, 1991
